h1: The 6 Best Lawn Mowers Under $500 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Lawn Mowers Under $500 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six lawn mowers under $500, covering 21-inch cordless, 80V self-propelled and gas models, with advice on lawn size and slopes.
summary: The EGO Power+ LM2114 is the best lawn mower under $500 for flat lawns: a 21 inch cordless deck with battery and charger in the box. The PowerSmart 21 inch gas mower with rear-wheel drive is the pick for hills. The Greenworks 80V adds self-propel to battery power, and the 16 inch Greenworks 40V suits small lawns.
intro: Around $500 the mower choice stops being about price and starts being about two decisions cheaper budgets never reach: does the machine drive its own wheels, and does it run on a battery or a gas engine? Plenty of buyers pay for propulsion they do not need on a flat quarter acre, while others skip it and spend every Saturday leaning into a slope.

We ranked six mowers that all land in the $200 to $500 bracket, working from spec sheets and owner descriptions. Deck width, drive type, power source and what ships in the box set the order. A battery mower sold without its battery and charger is not the bargain the sticker implies, and the extra purchase can erase the gap to a better machine.

products.name: EGO Power+ LM2114 21-Inch Cordless Mower
products.verdict: A full-width electric deck with the battery kit already in the box.
products.description:
The EGO Power+ LM2114 carries a full 21 inch deck with a cordless battery system, push drive, and both the battery and charger included in the box. Skipping gas means no oil changes, no stale fuel in spring and far less noise at 7 a.m. A 21 inch cut is the standard width, so you are not trading passes for convenience.

It leads because it combines the standard deck with a complete kit and almost no upkeep. The Greenworks 80V adds drive for a higher price, while the gas PowerSmart mowers need engine maintenance.

Buy it for a standard flat lawn where quiet, low-maintenance mowing matters. The caveat is propulsion: it is a push mower, so slopes tire you quickly, and skip it if your yard has hills or you want drive assistance.
products.idealFor: Standard flat lawns where quiet, low-upkeep mowing matters.
products.skipIf: Your yard has hills or you want drive assistance.

products.name: PowerSmart 21-Inch Gas Mower for Hills and Medium Yards
products.verdict: Rear-wheel drive traction for yards that are not flat.
products.description:
The PowerSmart 21 inch gas mower runs a 170cc OHV engine with rear-wheel self-propelled drive and six cutting height positions. Rear-wheel drive matters on hills, because weight shifts back as you climb, and rear wheels keep their grip where front-drive models slip.

It ranks second since gas engines need regular upkeep and run louder than the EGO. It beats the steel deck sibling on its purpose-built hill traction and the 22 inch model on cutting-height range, and it never stops for a battery.

Buy it for a hilly or uneven medium yard that needs grip. Skip it if you want zero fuel and engine maintenance. Plan on fresh fuel, oil changes on schedule and a spring tune-up.
products.idealFor: Hilly or uneven medium yards that need grip.
products.skipIf: You want zero fuel and engine maintenance.

products.name: PowerSmart 21-Inch Self-Propelled Gas Mower, Steel Deck
products.verdict: Similar gas power with a steel deck and three ways to handle clippings.
products.description:
The PowerSmart steel deck model also uses a 21 inch deck and a 170cc OHV engine with rear-wheel self-propel, but adds 3-in-1 operation: mulch, bag or discharge. A steel deck shrugs off sticks and stones that dent lighter material, and three clipping modes cover most lawn conditions.

It ranks third because it overlaps heavily with the model above, and the engine upkeep is the same. The steel deck and flexible clippings are the differences, and they matter for rough yards.

Buy it if you want steel and a choice of clipping handling. Skip it if you would rather avoid gas. If the lawn is hilly, the rear-wheel drive earns its keep, but both PowerSmart mowers need the same routine maintenance.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a steel deck and flexible clipping handling.
products.skipIf: You would rather avoid gas engines.

products.name: PowerSmart 22-Inch 170cc Self-Propelled Gas Mower
products.verdict: The widest cut here, with drive, at a lower cost than electric self-propel.
products.description:
The PowerSmart 22 inch mower is a 170cc gas, self-propelled machine with no battery or charging needed. At 22 inches it is the widest deck in the list, so a medium lawn takes fewer passes and less total time than a 21 inch model, and it is cheaper than the electric self-propelled option.

It ranks fourth because the listing offers fewer extras, with no stated height range or bagging details. The 21 inch PowerSmart models document more.

Buy it for a medium lawn where a wider cut saves time. Skip it if you want detail on height range or bagging. Gas upkeep applies, so keep fuel fresh and clean the deck after mowing. For larger lawns, a gas engine also avoids runtime limits.
products.idealFor: Medium lawns where a wider deck cuts mowing time.
products.skipIf: You want feature detail like height range or bagging.

products.name: Greenworks 80V 21-Inch Self-Propelled Mower
products.verdict: Battery power and drive assist, for a higher price.
products.description:
The Greenworks 80V 21 inch mower combines self-propelled drive with a 4.0Ah battery and charger included, no gas or fuel and a 21 inch deck. Battery drive gives you hill help without a pull cord, and 80V is the platform's high-power tier.

It ranks fifth because it costs the most of any mower under $500 here, and a single battery limits runtime on a larger lawn. The gas PowerSmart models cost less and never need a recharge.

Buy it for a medium to large lawn where you want drive without gas. Skip it if you are price-sensitive or want gas-style runtime. A second battery would extend coverage, but that adds to the real cost.
products.idealFor: Medium to larger lawns where you want drive without gas.
products.skipIf: You are price-sensitive or want gas-style runtime.

products.name: Greenworks 40V 16-Inch Push Mower
products.verdict: The lightest mower here, built for small flat lawns.
products.description:
The Greenworks 40V 16 inch push mower is the lightest mower in the guide, with a 4.0Ah battery and charger in the box, and it shares its battery with Greenworks 40V tools. Light weight makes it easy to haul out of a shed and store upright.

It ranks last because a 16 inch deck is the narrowest here, so you make noticeably more passes, and it is push only. Against the EGO, it covers less ground per pass.

Buy it for a small flat lawn, or if you already own Greenworks 40V tools and can share batteries. Skip it if your lawn is medium or larger, where the narrow deck costs time. Check battery runtime against your lawn size before buying.
products.idealFor: Small flat lawns and existing Greenworks 40V owners.
products.skipIf: Your lawn is medium or larger.

whatMatters.detail: Self-propelled mowers power their own wheels, while push mowers rely on you. On a flat lawn the difference is small, but on slopes it is large. Check the listing for the words self-propelled and whether the drive is front or rear wheel, since rear-wheel drive grips better uphill. The EGO LM2114 is push only, which suits a flat yard but not a slope.

Gas offers unlimited runtime with engine upkeep, while battery offers quiet, low upkeep and limited runtime. Your lawn size decides which wins. Look for engine cc, such as 170cc, or battery voltage and amp-hours, such as 80V and 4.0Ah, and compare them with the area you mow in one session and the time you want to spend.

Deck width is the cutting swath. A 21 inch deck is a common size, a 22 inch deck trims a few passes, and a 16 inch deck takes noticeably more. Compare the inch figure to your lawn size and the time you are willing to spend, because a narrow deck on a large lawn adds up quickly over a whole season.

Battery mowers vary on whether the battery and charger ship in the box. Buying them separately raises the real cost sharply, sometimes past the price of a gas mower. Read the listing for included battery details. The EGO, Greenworks 80V and Greenworks 40V here all include both, which is a point in their favor.

Hills and uneven ground need traction, which rear-wheel drive provides as weight shifts back on an incline. Flat lawns do not need it. Look for rear-wheel-drive wording if your yard slopes, and note that a heavier mower takes more effort to turn on a grade, so check the listed weight too.

faq.q: Do I need a self-propelled mower?
faq.a: On a flat, small lawn, usually not, because you can push it easily. On slopes or a medium yard it saves real effort. The PowerSmart models and Greenworks 80V offer it, while the EGO and Greenworks 40V are push only.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake at this budget?
faq.a: Skipping the included kit. All the battery mowers here ship with a battery and charger, so check that before comparing prices, because a bare tool needs a separate battery and charger purchase.

faq.q: Is battery worth it over gas?
faq.a: For a standard lawn, battery means no fuel or oil and less noise, as with the EGO LM2114. Gas, like the PowerSmart models, wins when runtime and slopes matter more than quiet.

faq.q: Can I use the Greenworks 40V battery elsewhere?
faq.a: It fits the Greenworks 40V tool platform, so owners of those tools can share it. Check compatibility on the listing before assuming a battery from another brand will fit, and keep the charger with it.

faq.q: How do I maintain a gas mower?
faq.a: Keep fuel fresh, change the oil on schedule and clean the deck after mowing. Check the manual for intervals on the PowerSmart models, and store with fuel handled as the maker advises, especially over winter.

faq.q: What if my lawn is bigger than a medium yard?
faq.a: Choose a gas model such as the PowerSmart 22 inch, or plan for extra battery capacity with a battery mower like the Greenworks 80V. A wider deck and unlimited runtime save time on bigger lawns.

finalTake: The EGO Power+ LM2114 is the right mower under $500 for most flat lawns, because it is quiet, complete in the box and easy to maintain. Pick the PowerSmart 21 inch gas model for hills, and the Greenworks 80V if you want battery with drive. Decide on slope and runtime first, then compare decks.
